description: .Net GPU compute for the browser and desktop. Write once, run on WebGPU, WebGL, Wasm, CUDA, OpenCL, and CPU.
releaseNotes:
v4.9.5-rc.26: WebGL body-struct codegen — closes the rc.25 v2 follow-ups, all 8 Tests23 body-struct tests now PASS on WebGL. Two additional fixes: (1) **Single-view body struct unwrap** — when a kernel parameter is a struct holding exactly one `ArrayView<T>` field (e.g. `Tests23_OnlyShortStruct { ArrayView<short> S0 }`), ILGPU's IR pre-transforms the param to the inner `ViewType<T>` directly, leaving the host side passing a struct value mismatched against a single-sampler kernel. `WebGLAccelerator.MarshalArguments` now walks struct args with no `BaseView` property; if the struct has exactly one IArrayView field it unwraps to that view, mirroring the IR transform. (2) **ArrayView1D wrapper metadata fields always intercepted** — a body struct of `ArrayView1D<T, Stride1D.Dense>` fields flattens in IR to (View, Int64-length, optional Int8-flag) per wrapper. Pre-rc.26 the codegen state machine used WGSL's `isLastField` heuristic to disambiguate length-vs-reduce-value, but in GLSL the standard `GenerateCode(GetField)` fallthrough then emitted `u_param{N}_stride[0]` for unmatched metadata fields — undeclared and broke compile. rc.26 unconditionally marks Int64-after-View as IsViewMetadata, the GetField hook intercepts all metadata fields and emits a length-uniform reference using the associated view's binding name (so `u_param{N}_f{metadata_fi}_length` aliases to `u_param{N}_f{view_fi}_length` which is actually declared). Together these close `Tests23_OnlyShortBodyStruct` and `Tests23_TwoShortBodyStructDense`. **All 8/8 WebGL body-struct tests PASS** including Tuvok's `Tests23_SilkBodyStructShape`. 12/12 desktop sweep clean (CUDA + OpenCL + CPU).

v4.9.5-rc.25: WebGL multi-view body-struct kernel parameter codegen (#26 partial close). When a kernel takes a struct parameter whose fields include 2+ `ArrayView<T>` (e.g. `Tests23_RegisterHeavyBody` with 12 ArrayView<int>, or Tuvok's `SilkDecodeCoreInputs` with 6 short + 9 int views), WebGL/GLSL now decomposes the body struct into per-field sampler bindings. Previous behavior: every field aliased the same single sampler, output was silently wrong. New behavior: each ArrayView field gets its own `u_param{N}_f{M}` sampler binding via a synthetic param-index encoding `(paramIdx+1)*1000 + fieldIdx`. Mirrors the WGSL pattern that shipped in rc.17/rc.18. **Verified PASSING on WebGL**: `Tests23_TwoShortBodyStruct`, `Tests23_SilkBodyStructShape` (Tuvok's actual 6 short + 9 int shape), `Tests23_RegisterHeavyBody_UnitExtent_NoLaunchFailure`, `Tests23_MinimalShortIntBodyStruct`, `Tests23_MinimalShortIntBodyStruct_IntOnly`, `Tests23_DeepUnroll_NoLaunchFailure`. **Known v2 follow-ups (still failing)**: `Tests23_OnlyShortBodyStruct` (single `ArrayView<short>` body field — buffer bind path issue) and `Tests23_TwoShortBodyStructDense` (`ArrayView1D<T, Stride1D.Dense>` body fields — IR multi-dim view path conflict). Workaround for both: use raw `ArrayView<T>` body fields with 2+ views, or pass single ArrayView as direct kernel param (not wrapped in struct).

v4.9.5-rc.24: CUDA body-struct ArrayView-field alignment ROOT-CAUSE FIX (#32 closed) + module-load diagnostics. (1) `IR.Types.ViewType.Alignment` was hardcoded to 4, so a body struct containing 2+ `ArrayView<T>` fields was emitted as `.param .align 4 .b8 _s_91[32]` in PTX. The host-side argument buffer was laid out at 8-byte alignment (each ArrayView field lowers to ViewImplementation = void* + long = 8-byte-aligned 16-byte struct), so the kernel signature alignment didn't match the buffer, and CUDA rejected the launch with `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_OUT_OF_RESOURCES` even at blockDim=1 — even though ptxas reported NUM_REGS=24, no spilling, no shared/local mem, MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK=1024. Single-ArrayView body structs and `ArrayView1D<T, Stride1D.Dense>` (which wraps the view in a StructureType) didn't trip the bug because their alignment propagated correctly via different paths. Fix: `ViewType` now mirrors `PointerType` — `Size = Alignment = 8` on 64-bit targets, 4 on 32-bit. Closes Tuvok's SilkDecodeCoreGpu CUDA bug (Tests23_SilkBodyStructShape, Tests23_TwoShortBodyStruct, Tests23_RegisterHeavyBody_UnitExtent_NoLaunchFailure, Tests23_RegisterHeavyBody_LargeExtent_Parallel all PASS post-fix on CUDA). (2) `CU_JIT_MAX_REGISTERS=255` cap added to `cuModuleLoadDataEx` (defense in depth — forces ptxas to spill instead of producing kernels that exceed the per-thread hardware cap on any sm_50+ device). Configurable via `CudaAccelerator.DefaultMaxRegistersPerThread` (default 255, set 0 to disable). (3) `CU_JIT_INFO_LOG_BUFFER` + `CU_JIT_LOG_VERBOSE` + `cuFuncGetAttribute` diagnostic plumbing — surfaces ptxas register/spill info and `MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK / NUM_REGS / SHARED_SIZE_BYTES / LOCAL_SIZE_BYTES / CONST_SIZE_BYTES / PTX_VERSION / BINARY_VERSION` per loaded kernel via `Trace.WriteLine` when `CudaAccelerator.VerboseModuleLoad = true` (off by default). (4) New regression `Tests23_DeepUnroll_NoLaunchFailure` locks down deep-unroll register-pressure shape across all backends.

v4.9.5-rc.23: Wasm dispatcher watchdog timeout. If worker tasks don't all complete within `WasmAccelerator.WasmDispatchWatchdogSeconds` (default 120s, set 0 to disable), throw a `TimeoutException` with kernel name, dispatch number, and completion ratio. Defense in depth atop rc.21's fast-fault — catches kernels that infinite-loop without erroring. Surfaced 2026-05-04 by Data's StyleMosaic Wasm hang where the kernel didn't trap, just never posted back.

v4.9.5-rc.22: WebGL runtime-safe Pow for negative base + buffer-loaded exponent. ONNX LayerNorm `(x-mean)^pow_initializer_2.0` has the exponent loaded from an ArrayView; static-const detection (rc.12) doesn't catch. Adds runtime-safe wrapper `(x>=0?pow(x,y):pow(abs(x),y)*(mod(y,2)>=1?-1:1))` for the buffer-loaded-exponent case. Closes Data's DistilBERT + SemanticSearch WebGL drift.

v4.9.5-rc.21: Wasm dispatcher fast-fault on first worker error + kernel name in error. `Task.WhenAll(workerTasks)` waited for ALL workers before throwing; one trap with others blocked = 10-min hang. Replaced with `Task.WhenAny` drain loop that throws on first faulted task. Worker error message now includes `kernel=<name>` so crew can identify the trapping op without per-dispatch diagnostic logging.

v4.9.5-rc.20: Wasm per-kernel worker module cache. Multi-kernel pipelines (ML inference: Conv2D / InstanceNorm / ReLU alternating) used to invalidate the worker-side `_cachedModule` on every kernel switch — 100 dispatches × 6 kernel types × 8 workers = ~4800 Wasm module re-compiles. Per-kernel cache: each (worker, kernel) compiles once and stays cached. Key: `kernelId = RuntimeHelpers.GetHashCode(wasmBytes)`.

v4.9.5-rc.19: WebGPU `WGSLTypeGenerator.GenerateTypeDefinitions` concurrent-modification fix. Iterating `mapping` while `this[fieldType]` lazily registered new types caused `InvalidOperationException: InvalidOperation_EnumFailedVersion`. Snapshot+drain pattern.

v4.9.5-rc.18: WebGPU WGSL IsMultiDim discriminates body struct from single ArrayView wrapper. A body struct with 2 × ArrayView1D = 6 IR fields was misclassified as 3D ArrayView; both views aliased to the same binding. Count actual ViewType fields to disambiguate.

v4.9.5-rc.17: WebGPU sub-word body-struct coalesce fix (closes Tuvok's SilkDecodeCoreGpu on WebGPU - task #33). `DecideCoalesceGroups` ran before `_subWordParams` was populated, so sub-word fields got bundled into a non-atomic int coalesce bucket and `atomicLoad` rejected the binding. Detect sub-word from `elemType.BasicValueType` directly.

v4.9.5-rc.16: Wasm snapshot invalidation perf — limit `_gpuWriteSeq` bump to actually-written buffers. Read-only ML weight buffers were being re-snapshotted every dispatch; 50MB × 100 dispatches = 5GB of wasted copies. Gate on `writtenBufferIndices.Contains(i)`.

v4.9.5-rc.15: Wasm dispatcher diagnostic typed-array allocations gated behind VerboseLogging. Hardcoded `length=4` in a debug block crashed sub-word body-struct kernels on first dispatch (when `bufferInfos[0]` was 2-byte short).

v4.9.5-rc.14: WebGL kernel-main override gets the Div/Rem unsigned cast and Pow neg-base int-exp expansion (the rc.12/rc.13 fixes only landed in the helper-function base; kernel-main override needed the same).

v4.9.5-rc.13: Two correctness fixes - Wasm dispatcher snapshot regression (BlazeFace/DDPM zero outputs at rc.11) + WGSL unsigned Div/Rem on i32-as-uint (closes DecodeUint on WebGPU).

v4.9.5-rc.12: WebGL GLSL Pow neg-base + integer exponent expansion (closes Data's DistilBERT/SemanticSearch/GPT-2 cluster) + WebGPU WGSL Shr/Shl signed-shift on i32-as-uint (closes Tuvok's DecodeBitLogP).

v4.9.5-rc.11: Wasm host-write-vs-queued-dispatch race fix. Snapshot SharedBuffer at queue time so D1's copy-IN reads its own data even if D2 host-overwrote between queues.

v4.9.5-rc.10: WebGL `glWorker.js` SubView-offset uniform leak across same-program dispatches (closes Data's StyleMosaic Gather + 11 ML cascade closures) + Wasm OOB diagnostic correctness (per-view element size tracking).

For older rc release notes, see git log on master and `_DevComms/global/nuget-local-publish-log.md`.
